Join our interdisciplinary team working at the intersection of Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, Explainable AI, and Automated Driving to shape the future of human-centered mobility systems.

The CARISSMA Institute of Automated Driving (C-IAD) at Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI), Germany, is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate in Driver Behavior Modeling to join our interdisciplinary research team working on human-centered automated driving and intelligent mobility systems.

Research Focus The successful candidate will contribute to the development of next-generation behavioral models for drivers and vulnerable road users (VRUs), combining cognitive science, machine learning, human factors, and automated driving research.

Your Responsibilities

• Develop cognitive models of driver and VRU decision-making based on psychological state and trait concepts.
• Design, conduct, and analyze user studies in driving simulators, mixed/virtual reality environments, and real-world traffic settings.
• Collect and analyze multimodal datasets including eye-tracking, psychophysiological measurements (e.g., EEG, ECG, GSR, SpO₂), motion capture, and behavioral data.
• Develop physical behavior models of VRUs (e.g., trajectories, body postures) and integrate cognitive factors into holistic behavioral models.
• Implement and advance machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) methods for behavior prediction and interpretation.
• Design, prototype, and evaluate novel human-machine interfaces for automated and connected mobility systems.
• Publish research findings in leading international journals and conferences.

Required Qualifications

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Human Factors, Psychology, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, or a related field.
• Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, C#, R) and experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
• Experience in experimental research and quantitative data analysis.
• Knowledge of psychophysiological sensing and signal processing (e.g., EEG, ECG, GSR, SpO₂) is desirable.
• Interest in explainable AI, human-machine interaction, and automated driving technologies.
• Very good English skills (C1 level or equivalent); German language skills (B2) are advantageous.
• Ability to work independently in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.

About the Position

• A fully funded PhD position until December 2029.
• Competitive salary according to the German public service scale (TV-L E13).
• Access to state-of-the-art research facilities, including driving simulators, VR/MR environments, eye-tracking systems, motion capture, and psychophysiological sensing equipment.
• Opportunities to collaborate with leading national and international research partners.
• Participation in high-impact research projects on automated driving, human-AI interaction, and intelligent mobility.
• Flexible working hours and home-office options.
• A modern workplace on the Ingolstadt campus, located in the heart of Bavaria’s automotive ecosystem.

Details and application (until July 13, 2026):
Applicants should submit a CV, academic transcripts, and a brief statement of research interests.
